person: Reggie Banks is 61, a retired grocery-chain AP clerk who now works three days a week doing finance for a small snack brand. The brand sells mostly through two distributors but also has a small Amazon FBA side channel of about 6 SKUs that nobody has time to audit. He has macular degeneration, works at 175% zoom with a high-contrast theme, and loses his place in wide tables, so he wants every claim shown as lines that add up. The founder wants one number: how much of the Amazon shortfall is real and recoverable. Reggie wants Athena to ask before anything is filed under the brand's account.
stated_up_front: I do the books for a snack brand and we have a few products on Amazon FBA that I've never checked for lost or short-received units. Could you go through last month's reports against our supplier's invoices and packing lists, and show me each claim line by line so I can add it up myself before anything gets filed?

facts.truth: 6 SKUs, all snack bars and trail-mix pouches; the biggest seller is the 12-count Peanut Crunch bar box.
About $140,000 a year, a small side channel next to the distributor business.
Harlan Valley Foods, a co-packer who emails invoices as PDFs to the shared brand inbox.
Brightline Fulfillment, which sends a packing list for every inbound shipment.
Inbound shipment sent 1,200 units of Peanut Crunch on invoice HV-4471, and Amazon's received count shows 1,140, so 60 units are short.
Peanut Crunch box costs $6.85 to make; the other five SKUs range from $4.10 to $7.90.

facts.about: Where he keeps his own tracking
facts.truth: An Excel workbook with one tab per month, one row per shipment, columns kept narrow enough to read at 175% zoom.

facts.about: Last time anyone looked at reimbursements
facts.truth: Nobody has audited since the spring; he thinks one small reimbursement of around $212 came through in August.
Reggie reviews, but the founder, Dana Whitcomb, has the Seller Central login and must be told before cases go in.
One number: the dollar total of Amazon's real shortfall, with the lines that add up to it.

unknowns: How long Amazon allows for opening a case on a lost or short-received inbound shipment.
Whether any of the shortages are the co-packer's fault rather than Amazon's, since he has not compared the 3PL packing lists to the invoices.
Whether a remeasure has already been used on any of his SKUs in the last 60 days.
What the codes in the inventory ledger's reason column mean.
